The National Parks are a vital part of the US. So, we need to continue to fight for them as they have been continuously attacked in the past year. 

Make sure to stay up to date on public land news and always speak up for our beautiful parks!

You NEED to do these underrated national park hikes in 2026! 😍

👉🏻 Follow @thegoodflawtravels for more bucket list national park hikes!

Over the past 4 years we have visited 21 national parks and these are our top 5 more underrated hikes that no one is talking about! 🤯

🥾 Tall Trees Grove in Redwood NP - 3.7 mile loop through one of the most remote parts of the park and takes you through some of the oldest, largest trees in the world. This hike REQUIRES a permit to do which you can get for free from at recreation.gov

🥾 Fairyland Loop in Bryce Canyon NP - 8 mile loop that takes you down into the canyon then back up to the rim and is located in one of the more secluded areas of the park. Seasonal road closures do impact getting to the trailhead so keep that in mind when planning!

🥾 Siyeh Pass in Glacier NP - 10 mile point to point that overlooks beautiful lakes and mountain ranges in the main part of the park. This is a great alternative to the Highline trail and way less crowded!

🥾 Cassidy Arch in Capitol Reef NP - 3.3 mile out and back that offers incredible views and takes you to one of the largest arches in the park. This trail is pretty popular and has no shade so you'll want to start early.

🥾 Surprise & Amphitheater Lake in Grand Teton NP - 10 miles out and back to two stunning lakes within the park that take you right up to the mountains. This trail branches into many other great hikes but overall was not super crowded and had some of the most incredible views!

⚠️ We highly recommend getting an America the Beautiful pass if you're planning to visit multiple parks in 2026 or pay attention to park entry fees when planning your trip! 

❤️ Please remember to leave no Trace when you're visiting these beautiful places!!
